title: Knowledge Check 8 - Lessons 36-40
description: Questions pooled from Lessons 36-40 - Data Enhancements, Sharing, and Analysis. Pass with 80% or higher to move toward unlocking the cert prep exam.

questions.question: A scenario needs a millisecond personalization decision based on the current page event, backed by a real-time data graph. Which insight type is appropriate?
options: Calculated Insight
Streaming Insight
Real-Time Insight
A copy field enrichment
questions.explanation: Real-time insights compute per event inside a real-time data graph with millisecond results, matching a live personalization decision, while calculated insights are batch and a copy field enrichment only displays data.

questions.question: Which statement about Data Actions is TRUE?
options: A data action edits the unified profile in place
A data action sends a payload to a target such as a Marketing Cloud Engagement data extension, the core platform, or a webhook
Data actions can only target a page layout
A data action replaces identity resolution
questions.explanation: Data actions deliver payloads to configured targets such as a data extension, the core platform, or a webhook, and they do not edit unified profiles, target page layouts, or substitute for identity resolution.

questions.question: A contact record page must show a single computed lifetime-value number copied from Data 360. Which enrichment type fits?
options: A related list enrichment, because it shows many rows
A copy field enrichment, because it copies a one-to-one value into a field
A direct-DMO related list
A data action
questions.explanation: Copy field enrichments copy field data from an object with a one-to-one relationship to a unified DMO into an org field, which is a single value, while related lists show many rows and data actions act rather than display.

questions.question: A contact record must show every email engagement from across the enterprise. Which reference path fits?
options: A copy field enrichment
A related list enrichment on a DMO with a one-to-many relationship to the unified individual
The Profile API on an engagement object
A page layout change alone
questions.explanation: A related list enrichment displays a DMO with a one-to-many relationship to the Individual or Unified Individual, which is exactly many email engagements, while copy fields need a one-to-one link, the Profile API excludes engagement objects, and a layout shows only org fields.

questions.question: A flow must read a pre-calculated, materialized view of related Data 360 data. What is the correct mechanism?
options: Add the data graph to the flow through its invocable action
Call the Profile API from the flow
Create a copy field enrichment
Turn off identity resolution
questions.explanation: A data graph is a materialized view that can be accessed through an invocable action in a flow, while the Profile API serves external profile queries, copy fields display single values, and identity resolution is unrelated.

questions.question: An external app needs to run Data 360 SQL across unified and engagement data model objects. Which API fits?
options: The Profile API, because it covers engagement objects
The Query API, which runs Data 360 SQL and supports data streams, profile, engagement, and unified objects
A related list enrichment
A data action target
questions.explanation: The Query API runs Data 360 SQL through the Data 360 Connect REST API and Apex and supports streams, profile, engagement, and unified objects, while the Profile API excludes engagement objects and enrichments and data action targets do not run ad hoc SQL.

questions.question: Which statement describes the source-of-truth relationship between Data 360 and the source systems?
options: Data 360 overwrites source records with reconciled values
Source systems stay authoritative for their own records, and Data 360 is the system of reference for the unified profile and computed insights
The source systems are deleted after unification
Copy field enrichments make the org the source of truth
questions.explanation: Unification links records and never overwrites them, so sources remain authoritative for their raw data while Data 360 references the unified and computed views, and copied values do not transfer authority.

questions.question: An architect needs a Data 360 value live on a record page with no local copy. Which approach matches that requirement?
options: A page layout change
A copy field enrichment that syncs on a schedule
A related list enrichment that reads the DMO through its lookup
A nightly export into a custom object
questions.explanation: A related list reads Data 360 data live through its lookup, so no local copy is created, while a copy field, an export, and a layout change all either duplicate the value or fail to surface Data 360 data.

questions.question: Which is the primary governance risk of copying unified data into org fields?
options: Data 360 credits are refunded
The unified profile is deleted
Identity resolution stops running
The copies diverge from the source and do not inherit Data 360 field-level security, so they can mislead users and expose sensitive data
questions.explanation: Copies drift from the source and carry only the destination field's own security, which risks both wrong values and exposure, while copying does not stop identity resolution, refund credits, or delete the unified profile.

questions.question: A consultant must report on a customer together with the source records that unified into that customer. Which approach is correct?
options: Build a standard report on the Unified Individual data model object only
Create a custom report type using the unified object as the primary object and relating the source object and the unified link object
Report on the raw data lake object
Copy the source records into a CRM custom object first
questions.explanation: The unified link object joins a unified profile to its contributing source records, which requires a custom report type relating the unified object, the source object, and the link object. A standard report reads a single object and cannot show the related source records.

questions.question: Which statement about standard versus custom Data 360 reports is TRUE?
options: A standard report can only be built on a calculated insight
A standard report can join up to four related data model objects
A custom report type can join up to four related data model objects, while a standard report reads a single object
Both report kinds write their output back to the data model objects
questions.explanation: A custom report type joins multiple related data model objects, up to four, using the lookup relationships, while a standard report is built on one object. Reports read data and present it; they never write back to the objects.

questions.question: A user with the correct license and the connector permission set cannot find a Data 360 object in the report builder. What is the most likely cause?
options: Data 360 reports cannot use unified objects
Bucket columns must be created before the object appears
The object has no page layout
The user lacks access to the underlying data model object, so it is not available to report on
questions.explanation: Report availability follows the sharing model of the underlying object, so a user who cannot see the data model object cannot report on it. Page layouts, unified object support, and bucket columns are unrelated to object availability in the builder.

questions.question: A stakeholder needs one view that shows a Data 360 unified customer metric next to CRM pipeline. Which surface fits best without extra architecture?
options: A standard Data 360 report on the unified object, which can also include CRM pipeline columns
A Lightning dashboard with one component on the Data 360 report and another component on the CRM report
A custom report type, because only custom report types can combine two sources
A calculated insight, because it blends Data 360 and CRM data automatically
questions.explanation: A Lightning dashboard combines components driven by different reports, so a Data 360 report and a CRM report can sit in one view. A standard report reads one object, a custom report type joins Data 360 objects, and a calculated insight computes metrics inside Data 360 rather than blending in CRM data.

questions.question: Which statement about the semantic layer is TRUE?
options: Semantic models remove the need for data model objects
A semantic model copies Data 360 data into a separate store
Semantic models define business meaning, relationships, and metrics over Data 360 objects and are reused across Salesforce
Semantic models can only be created in Tableau Desktop
questions.explanation: A semantic model is first-class Salesforce metadata that records which data model objects to use, how they relate, and the business definitions on top, and it is consumed by reports, Tableau Next, and AI. It does not copy data, is not limited to Tableau Desktop, and does not replace the data model objects it describes.

questions.question: A Data 360 report is shared as a dashboard but renders empty for the recipient. What is the most likely cause?
options: The report must be a custom report type
The dashboard is missing a bucket column
Dashboards cannot display Data 360 reports
The recipient lacks access to the underlying data model object, so the component shows nothing
questions.explanation: A dashboard inherits the viewer's access to the object and fields behind each report, so a recipient without access to the data model object sees an empty component. Dashboards do display Data 360 reports, and report kind or bucket columns do not cause an empty render.
